meta.note: Greek records are verified against the Evelyn-White (1914) Theogony. Norse and Egyptian records are still seeds (verified=false, no locators). roles and domains are editorial tags, not individually cited.

records.name: Gaia (Earth)

sources.claim: Comes into being right after Chaos and bears Heaven, hills and Pontus
Mother, by Heaven, of the Titans
Plots the attack on Heaven and arms Cronos with the sickle

records.summary: Earth comes into being right after Chaos and bears Heaven, the hills and Pontus. By Heaven she becomes the mother of the Titans, and later she plots against him and arms her son Cronus with the sickle.

records.name: Uranus (Heaven)

sources.claim: Born from Earth as her equal, to cover her on every side
Father of the Titans
Castrated by his son Cronos

records.summary: Heaven is born from Earth as her equal, to cover her on every side, and fathers the Titans with her. His own son Cronus castrates him.

records.name: Cronus

sources.claim: Youngest and most terrible of Earth and Heaven's children
Takes the sickle and castrates Heaven
Swallows his children to avoid being overthrown
Is tricked into vomiting them up again
Zeus is addressed as his son

records.summary: The youngest and most dreaded of the Titans, the children of Earth and Heaven. He takes the sickle and castrates his father, then swallows his own children to avoid being overthrown, until he is tricked into vomiting them up again. The Iliad addresses Zeus as his son.

records.name: Rhea

sources.claim: Listed among the Titans born to Earth and Heaven
Mother of the first Olympians; hides the infant Zeus on Crete
Sent by Zeus to Demeter, whom she calls her daughter

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven, and the mother of the first Olympians. She hides the infant Zeus on Crete. In the Hymn to Demeter Zeus sends her to Demeter, whom she calls her daughter.

records.name: Zeus

sources.claim: Youngest child of Cronos and Rhea, hidden on Crete
Overcomes Cronos and receives the thunderbolt
Leads the gods against the Titans
Defeats Typhoeus
Marriages and children of Zeus
Says he has not forgotten Odysseus, who sacrificed beyond all mortals
Praised in the opening hymn as the god who raises and humbles at will
Plans the evil that is the price of fire and sets the gods to make it
Supplicated by Thetis; addressed as son of Cronos
Bows his head to Thetis, wary of a quarrel with Hera
Declares that the descendant of Perseus about to be born will rule Mycenae
Takes Amphitryon's likeness and begets Heracles on Alcmena
Sends a storm on the Argo, angry at the murder of Apsyrtus
Father of Dionysus by Semele, who bore him secretly away from Hera; nods and makes Olympus reel
Gave Persephone to Aidoneus
Hades says he is the brother of Zeus
Sends Iris and then all the gods to win Demeter back
Welcomes Apollo into his house; Leto sits beside him
Bore Athena from his own head

records.summary: The youngest child of Cronus and Rhea, hidden on Crete as an infant. He overcomes his father, receives the thunderbolt, leads the gods against the Titans and defeats Typhoeus. The Theogony lists his marriages and children, and other poems name him as father of Dionysus, Heracles and Athena, whom he bears from his own head.

records.name: Hera

sources.claim: Named among the children of Cronos and Rhea
Zeus's last wife; mother of Hebe, Ares and Eileithyia
Bears Hephaestus without Zeus
Nourishes the Hydra, angry beyond measure at Heracles
Raised the Earthborn monsters as a trial for Heracles
Puts it in Achilles' heart to call the assembly, pitying the Danaans
Sends Athena to restrain Achilles
Confronts Zeus over his secret talk with Thetis
Hephaestus calls her his mother
Said to have prompted Jason's answer to Pelias, so that Medea would prove a curse to him
Helps the Argo pass the Clashing Rocks
Has the Ilithyias delay Alcmena's labour so that Eurystheus is born first
Sends two serpents to kill the infant Heracles
Pelias left her unhonoured; she loves Jason, who carried her across the river as an old woman
Spreads a mist so the heroes reach the palace unseen
Arranges for Medea to go to Iolcus as a bane to Pelias
Keeps Eilithyia on Olympus out of envy while Leto labours
Angry that Zeus bore Athena alone; recalls casting out her lame son Hephaestus
Bears Typhaon without Zeus and gives him to the dragoness

records.summary: A daughter of Cronus and Rhea and the last wife of Zeus in the Theogony's list, mother of Hebe, Ares and Eileithyia, and of Hephaestus, whom she bears without Zeus. She is hostile to Heracles: she raises the Hydra against him, sends two serpents to his cradle and has his birth delayed. She helps Jason, whom she loves for carrying her across a river.

records.name: Poseidon

sources.claim: Named among the children of Cronos and Rhea (as the Earth-Shaker)
Husband of Amphitrite and father of Triton
Rages against Odysseus for blinding his son the Cyclops Polyphemus
Named with Hera and Athena among the gods who wished to bind Zeus
sources.note: Reported by Achilles, quoting Thetis. The attempt itself is not narrated in Book 1.

sources.claim: Father of Pegasus and Chrysaor by Medusa
Jason dedicates the Argo to him at the Isthmus

records.summary: A child of Cronus and Rhea, called the Earth-Shaker, husband of Amphitrite and father of Triton. Apollodorus makes him the father of Pegasus and Chrysaor by Medusa. In the Odyssey he rages against Odysseus for blinding his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus.

records.name: Hades

sources.claim: Named among the children of Cronos and Rhea
Rules the halls of the underworld with Persephone
Carries off Persephone
Carries off Persephone with the leave of Zeus
Helios calls him a fitting husband for her, as her father's brother and Demeter's brother
Calls himself the brother of Zeus and a fitting husband for Persephone

records.summary: A child of Cronus and Rhea who rules the halls of the underworld. He carries off Persephone with the leave of Zeus. In the Hymn to Demeter he calls himself the brother of Zeus and a fitting husband for her.

records.name: Demeter

sources.claim: Named among the children of Cronos and Rhea
Bears Persephone to Zeus
Bears Plutus to Iasion on Crete
Mother of Persephone, who was given to Hades by Zeus
Angry with Zeus, she leaves Olympus
Withholds the crops until Zeus yields
Rhea calls her "my daughter" and brings Zeus's offer

records.summary: A child of Cronus and Rhea. She bears Persephone to Zeus and Plutus to Iasion on Crete. When Zeus gives Persephone to Hades, she leaves Olympus in anger and withholds the crops until Zeus yields.

records.name: Hestia

sources.claim: First-named child of Cronos and Rhea

records.summary: The first-named child of Cronus and Rhea. The passages read so far say little else about her.

records.name: Athena

sources.claim: Her mother Metis is swallowed by Zeus before the birth
Born from Zeus's own head
Dresses the first woman
Urges Tiphys to join and fashions the Argo with Argus
Gave Jason the purple mantle when the ship was begun
Pleads for Odysseus before Zeus
Proposes to send Hermes to Calypso and goes to Ithaca herself
Ordered to teach the first woman needlework; clothes and adorns her
Sent by Hera to stay Achilles' sword, and he obeys
Advises Argus on building the Argo and fits a speaking timber at its prow
Guides Perseus's hand as he beheads Medusa
Gives Heracles bronze castanets she had from Hephaestus
Confers with Hera on how to help the heroes, and goes with her to Aphrodite
Fashioned the Argo, as Argus tells Aeetes
Tore the dragon's teeth from its jaws and gave half to Aeetes
Born from the head of Zeus, to the anger of Hera

records.summary: Born from the head of Zeus after he swallows her mother Metis, to the anger of Hera. She teaches and dresses the first woman, helps build the Argo, pleads for Odysseus before Zeus, guides Perseus's hand against Medusa, and gives Heracles bronze castanets against the Stymphalian birds.

records.name: Apollo

sources.claim: Son of Leto and Zeus
Jason prays to him at the altar; he had promised guidance at Pytho
Leto bore him on the seventh of the month
Son of Leto and Zeus; sends a plague on the Achaeans
Comes down from Olympus and strikes the army with arrows
Holds the lyre at the gods' feast
Flashes lightning from the Melantian ridges; the Argonauts found an altar to Radiant Apollo at Anaphe
Leto bears him and Artemis; the gods tremble before him, but Leto sits beside Zeus
Leto labours nine days on Delos while Hera keeps Eilithyia away; Apollo is born
Plays the lyre among the gods on Olympus
Shoots the dragoness who fostered Typhaon
Tells the Cretans he is the son of Zeus

records.summary: The son of Leto and Zeus, born on Delos after Hera keeps Eilithyia away from Leto's labour. In the Iliad he sends a plague on the Achaeans. He plays the lyre among the gods, and in the Hymn to Apollo he shoots the dragoness that fostered Typhaon. Jason prays to him before the voyage of the Argo.

records.name: Artemis

sources.claim: Daughter of Leto and Zeus
Twin of Apollo, born to Leto in Ortygia
Sings among the gods; sister of Apollo

records.summary: The daughter of Leto and Zeus and the twin of Apollo, born in Ortygia. She sings among the gods on Olympus in the Hymn to Apollo.

records.name: Leto

sources.claim: Daughter of Phoebe and Coeus
Bears Apollo and Artemis to Zeus
Bore Apollo on the seventh of the month
Named as the mother of Apollo
Mother of Apollo and Artemis, born on Delos
Labours nine days on Delos while Hera keeps Eilithyia away

records.summary: The daughter of Phoebe and Coeus, and the mother of Apollo and Artemis by Zeus. She labours for nine days on Delos while Hera keeps Eilithyia away.

records.name: Hermes

sources.claim: Son of Maia and Zeus; herald of the gods
Ordered to give the first woman a shameless mind and a deceitful nature
Sent to bring her to Epimetheus
Guides Perseus and gives him an adamantine sickle
Jason carries Hermes' wand
Father of the Argonaut Aethalides
Sent by Zeus to Erebus to bring Persephone back to her mother

records.summary: The son of Maia and Zeus and herald of the gods. He is ordered to give the first woman a deceitful nature and sent to bring her to Epimetheus, is sent by Zeus to bring Persephone back from the underworld, and guides Perseus and gives him an adamantine sickle.

records.name: Ares

sources.claim: Son of Hera and Zeus
Father, with Aphrodite, of Panic, Fear and Harmonia

records.summary: The son of Hera and Zeus, and the father, with Aphrodite, of Panic, Fear and Harmonia. The passages read so far say little else about him.

records.name: Aphrodite

sources.claim: Rises from the foam around Heaven's severed members
Bears Panic, Fear and Harmonia to Ares
Ordered to shed grace and cruel longing on the first woman's head
Hera and Athena ask her to send Eros against Medea; she agrees to coax him
Wife of the lame god Hephaestus, who built her palace
Called a daughter of Zeus, dancing on Olympus
sources.note: Differs from the Theogony (ll. 176-206), where she rises from the foam around the severed members of Heaven.

records.summary: In the Theogony she rises from the foam around the severed members of Heaven, while the Hymn to Apollo calls her a daughter of Zeus. She bears Panic, Fear and Harmonia to Ares. In the Argonautica she is the wife of Hephaestus and agrees to send Eros against Medea when Hera and Athena ask.

records.name: Hephaestus

sources.claim: Born to Hera without Zeus; the most skilled craftsman of the gods
Forms the first woman from earth
Marries Aglaea, youngest of the Graces
Ordered by Zeus to mould the first woman from earth and water, and fashions her from clay
Son of Hera; recalls being hurled from heaven by Zeus; pours wine for the gods
Built a palace for each of the gods
Husband of Aphrodite; built her palace and works at his forge
Made the bronze-footed bulls and the plough for Aeetes, and the fountains in his palace
Hera's weakly, lame son whom she threw into the sea; raised by Thetis

records.summary: Born to Hera without Zeus and the most skilled craftsman of the gods. He forms the first woman from clay, built a palace for each god and made bronze-footed bulls for Aeetes. In the Iliad he recalls being hurled from heaven by Zeus, and in the Hymn to Apollo Hera tells how she cast him out. His wife is Aglaea in the Theogony and Aphrodite in the Argonautica.

records.name: Dionysus

sources.claim: Son of Zeus and the mortal Semele; now a god
Marries Ariadne, who is made immortal
Son of Zeus and Semele, born away from Hera

records.summary: The son of Zeus and the mortal Semele, born away from Hera and now a god. He marries Ariadne, who is made immortal.

records.name: Persephone

sources.claim: Daughter of Demeter and Zeus; carried off by Hades
Queen of the underworld beside Hades
Demeter's daughter, carried off by Aidoneus with the leave of Zeus
Hades promises her honour as his wife and queen of the dead
Tells her mother how she was taken and made to eat the pomegranate seed

records.summary: The daughter of Demeter and Zeus, carried off by Hades with the leave of Zeus. She becomes queen of the underworld beside him, and tells her mother how she was taken and made to eat the pomegranate seed.

records.name: Prometheus

sources.claim: Son of Iapetus and Clymene; bound by Zeus, later freed by Heracles
Tricks Zeus over the sacrifice, steals fire, and is punished
Zeus hides fire because Prometheus deceived him; Prometheus steals it back in a fennel stalk
Zeus answers by promising men an evil as the price of fire
Offers himself to Zeus to take over Chiron's immortality, so that Chiron can die
The plant used in the "charm of Prometheus" sprang from his blood as the eagle tore him on the Caucasus

records.summary: A Titan, the son of Iapetus and Clymene. He tricks Zeus over the sacrifice and steals fire. Zeus punishes him by binding him and by sending an evil to mankind as the price of fire, and Heracles later kills the eagle and frees him. Apollodorus has him take over Chiron's immortality, and a plant used in Medea's charm springs from his blood.

records.name: Calypso

sources.claim: Listed among the daughters of Ocean and Tethys
Joined to Odysseus in love; bears Nausithous and Nausinous
Keeps Odysseus in her hollow caves, wanting him as her husband
Described by Athena as the daughter of Atlas who holds Odysseus on her island

records.summary: Listed among the daughters of Ocean and Tethys, though Athena calls her the daughter of Atlas. She keeps Odysseus on her island, wanting him as her husband, and in the Theogony bears him two sons, Nausithous and Nausinous.

records.name: Chaos

sources.claim: The first thing to come into being, before Earth; Erebus and Night come forth from it

records.summary: The first thing to come into being in the Theogony, before Earth. Erebus and black Night come forth from it.

records.name: Tartarus

sources.claim: Comes into being in the depths of the wide-pathed Earth
The defeated Titans are bound beneath the earth as far down as Tartarus, behind a bronze fence and a triple line of night
Father of Typhoeus by Earth; Zeus hurls the monster into wide Tartarus

records.summary: A dim region deep in the earth that comes into being early in the Theogony. The defeated Titans are bound there behind a bronze fence, and Zeus hurls Typhoeus into it. Tartarus is also named as the father of Typhoeus, by Earth.

records.name: Eros (Love)

sources.claim: Among the first to come into being; the fairest of the deathless gods, who overcomes the mind and counsel of gods and men
Goes with Aphrodite at her birth and joins the assembly of the gods
Hera and Athena ask Aphrodite to send him against Medea
His arrow strikes Medea with love for Jason

records.summary: One of the first beings to come into being, called the fairest of the deathless gods, who overcomes the minds of gods and men. He goes with Aphrodite at her birth. In the Argonautica Hera and Athena ask Aphrodite to send him against Medea, and his arrow strikes her with love for Jason.

records.name: Nyx (Night)

sources.claim: Comes from Chaos; with Erebus she bears Aether and Day
Bears Doom, Fate, Death, Sleep and the Dreams, and, though she lay with none, Blame, Woe, the Hesperides, the Fates and Nemesis
Her house stands where Night and Day pass each other at the bronze threshold; she holds Sleep in her arms

records.summary: Black Night comes from Chaos and, with Erebus, bears Aether and Day. She bears Doom, Fate, Death, Sleep and the Dreams, and, though she lay with none, Blame, Woe, the Hesperides, the Fates and Nemesis. Her house stands where Night and Day pass each other at a bronze threshold.

records.name: Pontus (Sea)

sources.claim: Earth bears him, the barren raging sea, without any union of love
Fathers Nereus, the eldest, and with Earth also Thaumas, Phorcys, Ceto and Eurybia

records.summary: The barren, raging sea, borne by Earth without any union of love. He fathers Nereus, the eldest of his children, and with Earth also Thaumas, Phorcys, Ceto and Eurybia.

records.name: Thanatos (Death)

sources.claim: A child of Night
Sleep is called his brother
Lives with Sleep where the sun never looks; has a heart of iron, holds fast whomever he seizes, and is hateful even to the gods

records.summary: A child of Night who lives with his brother Sleep in the dark where the sun never looks. He has a heart of iron, and whomever he has seized he holds fast. Even the gods hate him.

records.name: Hypnos (Sleep)

sources.claim: A child of Night
Called the brother of Death; Night holds him in her arms
Roams peacefully over earth and sea and is kind to men

records.summary: A child of Night and the brother of Death. He roams peacefully over the earth and the sea and is kind to men.

records.name: Oceanus

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Tethys bears him the rivers
With Tethys the father of three thousand daughters, among them Styx, Metis, Calypso, Idyia and Perseis
A branch of his stream feeds the Styx, whose water is the gods' great oath

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. Tethys bears him the rivers and three thousand daughters, among them Styx, Metis, Calypso, Idyia and Perseis. A branch of his stream feeds the Styx, whose water is the gods' great oath.

records.name: Tethys

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Bears Ocean the rivers
With Ocean the mother of three thousand daughters, the eldest of them named in a long list

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. She bears Ocean the rivers and, with him, three thousand daughters.

records.name: Hyperion

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Theia bears him Helius, Selene and Eos

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. With Theia he is the father of the Sun, the Moon and Dawn.

records.name: Theia

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Subject in love to Hyperion, she bears Helius, Selene and Eos

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. With Hyperion she is the mother of the Sun, the Moon and Dawn.

records.name: Themis

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Zeus marries her; she bears the Hours and the Fates

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. Zeus marries her, and she bears the Hours and the Fates.

records.name: Mnemosyne (Memory)

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Bears the nine Muses to Zeus in Pieria after nine nights
Zeus loves her and the nine Muses are born

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven, who reigns over the hills of Eleuther. Zeus lies with her for nine nights and she bears the nine Muses.

records.name: Coeus

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Phoebe comes to his embrace and bears Leto and Asteria

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. With Phoebe he is the father of Leto and Asteria.

records.name: Phoebe

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Comes to the embrace of Coeus and bears Leto and Asteria

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. With Coeus she is the mother of Leto and Asteria.

records.name: Iapetus

sources.claim: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven
Marries Clymene; their sons are Atlas, Menoetius, Prometheus and Epimetheus

records.summary: A Titan, born to Earth and Heaven. He marries Clymene, and their sons are Atlas, Menoetius, Prometheus and Epimetheus.

records.name: Atlas

sources.claim: Son of Iapetus and Clymene; by Zeus's assignment he holds up the wide heaven at the edge of the earth
Stands before the house of Night holding up heaven
Father of Maia
Athena calls him the father of Calypso
sources.note: Differs from the Theogony, which lists Calypso among the daughters of Ocean.

records.summary: A son of Iapetus and Clymene who, by Zeus's assignment, holds up the wide heaven at the edge of the earth. Maia is his daughter. In the Odyssey Athena calls Calypso his daughter, where the Theogony lists her among the daughters of Ocean.

records.name: Epimetheus

sources.claim: Son of Iapetus; from the first a mischief to men, since he was the first to take from Zeus the woman he had formed
The first woman is sent to him

records.summary: A son of Iapetus and Clymene and brother of Prometheus. He is called a mischief to men because he was the first to take the woman Zeus had formed, whom Hermes brings to him in Works and Days.

records.name: Menoetius

sources.claim: Son of Iapetus; Zeus strikes him with a thunderbolt and sends him down to Erebus for his presumption

records.summary: A son of Iapetus and Clymene. Zeus strikes him with a thunderbolt and sends him down to Erebus for his presumption.

records.name: Helios (Sun)

sources.claim: Born to Hyperion and Theia, with Selene and Eos
Father of Circe and Aeetes by Perseis
Circe is called the daughter of Helius, Hyperion's son

records.summary: The Sun, born to Hyperion and Theia with the Moon and Dawn. By Perseis he is the father of Circe and Aeetes.

records.name: Eos (Dawn)

sources.claim: Born to Hyperion and Theia; she shines on all on earth and on the gods
Bears the winds Zephyrus, Boreas and Notus, and the star Eosphorus, to Astraeus
Bears Memnon and Emathion to Tithonus and Phaethon to Cephalus

records.summary: Dawn, born to Hyperion and Theia, who shines on all on earth and on the gods. She bears the winds Zephyrus, Boreas and Notus to Astraeus, and sons to the mortals Tithonus and Cephalus.

records.name: Hecate

sources.claim: Zeus honours her above all and gives her a share of earth, sea and heaven; she favours kings in judgement, warriors, athletes, horsemen and fishermen, and nurses the young
Medea is her priestess

records.summary: A goddess whom Zeus honours above all, giving her a share of earth, sea and heaven. She aids those she favours in judgement, battle, games and at sea, and is a nurse of the young. In the Argonautica Medea is her priestess.

records.name: Styx

sources.claim: The chiefest of the daughters of Ocean and Tethys
Bears Zelus, Nike, Cratos and Bia to Pallas; first to Olympus to back Zeus against the Titans, and Zeus makes her the great oath of the gods
Lives apart in a rock-vaulted house; Iris fetches her water for the gods' oath, and a god who swears falsely is cut off from the others for years

records.summary: The eldest daughter of Ocean. She is the first to join Zeus on Olympus against the Titans, and he makes her the great oath of the gods. Iris fetches her water for the oath, and a god who swears falsely is cut off from the others for years.

records.name: Metis

sources.claim: Listed among the daughters of Ocean and Tethys
Zeus's first wife and the wisest of gods and mortals; he swallows her before she bears Athena, on the advice of Earth and Heaven
She conceives Pallas Athene and stays inside Zeus, who gives birth to Athena through his head

records.summary: A daughter of Ocean and the first wife of Zeus, wisest among gods and mortals. Because Earth and Heaven advise that her children would threaten Zeus, he swallows her before she bears Athena, and Athena is later born from his head.

records.name: Aglaea

sources.claim: One of the three Graces, daughters of Zeus and Eurynome
The youngest of the Graces; Hephaestus makes her his wife

records.summary: The youngest of the three Graces, daughters of Zeus and Eurynome. Hephaestus makes her his wife.

records.name: The Muses

sources.claim: Nine daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne, born in Pieria
Named as Cleio, Euterpe, Thaleia, Melpomene, Terpsichore, Erato, Polyhymnia, Urania and Calliope; with Apollo they make singers and harpers, and they favour princes
Born from Zeus and Mnemosyne

records.summary: Nine daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne, born in Pieria, named as Cleio, Euterpe, Thaleia, Melpomene, Terpsichore, Erato, Polyhymnia, Urania and Calliope. Through them and Apollo there are singers and harpers on earth, and they favour wise princes.

records.name: The Fates (Moerae)

sources.claim: Born of Night: Clotho, Lachesis and Atropos, who give men good and evil at birth and punish the transgressions of men and gods
Also said to be born of Zeus and Themis, who gives them the greatest honour
sources.note: Differs from ll. 211-225, where Night bears them.

records.summary: Clotho, Lachesis and Atropos, who give men both good and evil at their birth and pursue the transgressions of men and gods. The Theogony says in one place that Night bore them and in another that Zeus and Themis did.

records.name: Nereus

sources.claim: The eldest child of Sea; truthful and gentle, called the Old Man
Father, by Doris, of fifty daughters

records.summary: The eldest child of Sea, called the Old Man because he is truthful and gentle. With Doris he is the father of fifty daughters, among them Amphitrite and Thetis.

records.name: Thetis

sources.claim: One of the fifty daughters of Nereus and Doris
The silver-shod goddess, subject to Peleus, bears Achilles
Raised Hephaestus after Hera threw him into the sea
Supplicates Zeus

records.summary: One of the fifty daughters of Nereus. She bears Achilles to the mortal Peleus, and in the Iliad she supplicates Zeus. In the Hymn to Apollo she raises Hephaestus after Hera throws him into the sea.

records.name: Amphitrite

sources.claim: One of the daughters of Nereus; with Cymodoce she calms the waves
Wife of Poseidon and mother of Triton

records.summary: One of the daughters of Nereus, who with Cymodoce calms the waves. She is the wife of Poseidon and the mother of Triton.

records.name: Triton

sources.claim: Son of Amphitrite and Poseidon; owns the depths of the sea and lives with his parents in a golden house

records.summary: The son of Amphitrite and Poseidon, who owns the depths of the sea and lives with his parents in a golden house.

records.name: Iris

sources.claim: The swift daughter of Thaumas and Electra, and sister of the Harpies
Zeus sends her to fetch the water of the Styx in a golden jug
Zeus sends her to win Demeter back

records.summary: The swift daughter of Thaumas and Electra and sister of the Harpies. Zeus sends her as messenger, to fetch the water of the Styx for the gods' oath and, in the Hymn to Demeter, to call Demeter back.

records.name: Phorcys

sources.claim: A child of Sea, born when Sea mated with Earth
Father, by Ceto, of the Graiae and the Gorgons, among them Medusa

records.summary: A child of Sea and Earth. With Ceto he is the father of the Graiae and the Gorgons, among them Medusa.

records.name: Ceto

sources.claim: A child of Sea, born when Sea mated with Earth
Mother, by Phorcys, of the Graiae and the Gorgons, among them Medusa

records.summary: A child of Sea and Earth. With Phorcys she is the mother of the Graiae and the Gorgons, among them Medusa.
